title: Prove eight-width Clifford tests and compact exact native certificates
body:
A complete native identity can fail beyond the tensor widths that were sampled. This PR gives a finite test for all positive widths, a quantitative failure bound, and exact certificates that do not allocate dense base or tensor matrices. The class is the full dyadic Clifford group, including the source Gaussian and Hadamard gates. **There is no improvement to the complete kappa calculation.**

The [original proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5370f4465388dbbfff3ba45d5d6ae99d447b1766/research/clifford-tensor-gram/PROOF.md) and [extensions](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5370f4465388dbbfff3ba45d5d6ae99d447b1766/research/clifford-tensor-gram/ADVANCES.md) establish four results:

- On `n >= 2` binary axes, equality at the **eight widths 8n-3 through 8n+4** is equivalent to equality at every positive width. For nine axes, the test uses widths **69 through 76**. The maximum general cutoff remains 8n+4. For zero axes use widths 1,2,3,4.
- On one axis, **widths 5,6,7,8 suffice**. The [rank-96 inverse certificate](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5370f4465388dbbfff3ba45d5d6ae99d447b1766/research/clifford-tensor-gram/ONE-AXIS-RANK.json) proves sufficiency. The [Reynolds example](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5370f4465388dbbfff3ba45d5d6ae99d447b1766/research/clifford-tensor-gram/examples/reynolds.certificate.json) passes widths 1 through 7 and fails at 8 with entry 5/24. Thus the maximum cutoff eight is sharp. Central phase residues also show that four tests are necessary.
- For distinct exact operators with squared coefficient norm `M`, some width in **1 through 8n+4** has normalized squared Hilbert-Schmidt residual at least **(75/76)M**, improving 14/15. This constant is not claimed for only the eight selected widths.
- The [compact producer](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5370f4465388dbbfff3ba45d5d6ae99d447b1766/research/clifford-tensor-gram/compact.py) uses [phase-exact quadratic sums](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5370f4465388dbbfff3ba45d5d6ae99d447b1766/research/clifford-tensor-gram/quadratic.py) for native entries, traces and conditional inner products. A bitwise witness search replaces the old scan of all `D^2` coordinate pairs. Work is polynomial in the expanded support, literal word length, axis count and tested width. Expanded support can still be exponential in program length.

The [guide](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5370f4465388dbbfff3ba45d5d6ae99d447b1766/research/clifford-tensor-gram/README.md), [continuation receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5370f4465388dbbfff3ba45d5d6ae99d447b1766/research/clifford-tensor-gram/ADVANCES-RESULT.json), [research notes](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5370f4465388dbbfff3ba45d5d6ae99d447b1766/research/clifford-tensor-gram/RESEARCH-NOTES.md) and [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5370f4465388dbbfff3ba45d5d6ae99d447b1766/research/clifford-tensor-gram/SOURCES.json) provide the entry points. Saved large examples certify a [64-axis failure](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5370f4465388dbbfff3ba45d5d6ae99d447b1766/research/clifford-tensor-gram/examples/native-64.certificate.json) with literal entry 1/4294967296 and a [65-axis native phase identity](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5370f4465388dbbfff3ba45d5d6ae99d447b1766/research/clifford-tensor-gram/examples/native-65.certificate.json). Their base dimensions are 2^64 and 2^65. These are explicit fixtures, not complete provider runs.

This is an **enabling proof and algorithmic improvement**. Operators are unitary matrices over `Z[i,1/2]` that normalize the Pauli group. Exact global phases remain inside tensor powers. All dirty inputs and returns are independent. Programs and scalar coefficients are fixed as width varies. The proof permits complex coefficients; the implementation uses exact Gaussian rationals. Width-dependent programs, non-Clifford or nonunitary native operators, restricted clean inputs, rectangular types and nonlinear or rounded leaves are outside the contract. No fast general circuit solver or practical full-provider speedup is claimed.

Validation used CPython 3.12.13 on macOS and the standard library:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-tensor-gram
python3.12 -I -B research/clifford-tensor-gram/audit_mutations.py
python3.12 -I -B research/clifford-tensor-gram/audit_advances.py
```

The registered runner passes the original and continuation replays in normal and optimized modes. They print `PASS_CLIFFORD_TENSOR_GRAM_NO_NEW_KAPPA` and `PASS_CLIFFORD_ADVANCES_NO_NEW_KAPPA`, then the runner prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/clifford-tensor-gram outcome=completed`. The two audits print `PASS_CLIFFORD_GRAM_MUTATIONS` and `PASS_CLIFFORD_ADVANCE_MUTATIONS`.

The continuation checks 256 code Fourier values, filter bounds through 64 axes, the modular inverse by matrix multiplication, 640 exhaustive small quadratic sums, 3,328 native entries, 128 traces, 304 partial inner products, 48 complete programs and literal witnesses, nine exact native relations, a scalar-phase trap and eight rejection controls. The [original receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5370f4465388dbbfff3ba45d5d6ae99d447b1766/research/clifford-tensor-gram/RESULT.json) also remains unchanged after the integer filter optimization. The compact compiler reuses the original signed-word expander; its differential oracles are the separate dense compiler and frozen native matrices. It is not an independent checker of itself.

The [original mutations](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5370f4465388dbbfff3ba45d5d6ae99d447b1766/research/clifford-tensor-gram/MUTATIONS.json) and [continuation mutations](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5370f4465388dbbfff3ba45d5d6ae99d447b1766/research/clifford-tensor-gram/ADVANCES-MUTATIONS.json) reject eight mathematical defects in both Python modes, for 16 negative runs. Committed-byte checks and official 35-file export integrity pass. All four replays pass in a fresh read-only export with Git absent from PATH; all 36 regular files, including its manifest, remain unchanged. Export SHA-256: `67414cafa95073d295ae100dc2868d254e233d83759f8c4212bd384087108cf9`.

Finite checks corroborate the written proofs. No independent human review, proof-kernel acceptance, complete current provider, selected cold replay, Lean or Docker run is claimed. Physical ownership, storage, stock, precision, tapes and outer recovery remain separate obligations. The optional full-history preflight was omitted in this shallow checkout; exact source objects and bytes were checked, and the declared base is an ancestor of the contribution.

Scientific base: canonical main `7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56`, priority revision 7. Exact contribution head: `5370f4465388dbbfff3ba45d5d6ae99d447b1766`. Both consumed kernels retain their original pins. The continuation and submission refreshes reached `1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4`; priorities and both dependencies are unchanged. The [selected conditional kappa](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1ec1119972c9aefe42525172d07b332fcff81cb4/certificates/selected-result.json) is 15108879/5000000000, from separate maintainer work. This PR changes no selected record or predecessor package.

The final advisory overlap refresh covers 337 open PRs and 4,676 Discussion records, with complete remote pagination. The sparse local inventory and arbitrary historical diffs are coverage limits. Related source proofs and the concurrent monomial PR head were checked separately. The [canonical claim and handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5236#discussioncomment-19153620) records the scope.

Credit and distinctions:

- Rohan Arun and the retained native lineage supply the exact kernel, retained by Tekalign (@tekuuu). Jeremy Kothe, Cinna Davis (@1337isnot1337) and the other source authors keep their credit in the [unchanged notice](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/5370f4465388dbbfff3ba45d5d6ae99d447b1766/research/clifford-tensor-gram/vendor/NATIVE-LINEAGE-NOTICE).
- @zxv supplied the independent-operator interface and frozen arithmetic in [PR #5235](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5235). @krzysztofwojt supplied the inverse interface and native-relation handoff in [PR #5262](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5262).
- lm1909's [projection note](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56/research/projection-recursion-check/README.md), following Jacob Alan Sussman's engine model, already uses positive-width group separation. @Clear1nsight supplied related finite-alphabet arguments in [PR #4928](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4928) and [PR #4978](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4978). The [general separation proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56/research/two-full-retained-helper-ceiling/science/PROOF.md) and [passive-query clarification](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56/research/passive-saved-query-ceiling/evidence/frozen/pr4948-saved-query-macro-gate/UNIFORM-ALPHABET-ADDENDUM.md) retain their wider coefficient quantifiers.
- Concurrent [PR #5369](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5369) proves a four-width criterion for affine-quadratic monomial maps, with a central-residue obstruction. Its scope excludes Hadamard gates. Its proof, complexity result and event fixture remain separate and unchanged.
- The code invariant is classical work of Runge, as credited in [Nebe, Rains and Sloane](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0001038). Binary quadratic representations of Clifford operations are classical work of [Dehaene and De Moor](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0304125). The extension proof derives the native phases explicitly. No general stabilizer-simulation or global literature priority is claimed.

New work by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. Remaining questions are a sharp cutoff for multiple axes, stability on only the eight selected widths, and support growth in a complete provider.
